en.name: Shimeji
en.summary: Shimeji are the small-capped mushrooms sold as a joined cluster on a block of growing medium, firm and mildly nutty when cooked. No figure is published for them, so treat them like mushrooms generally: about 5–7 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: Shimeji should not be kept at room temperature. Like any fresh mushroom they respire and sweat, and warmth softens the caps and starts the surface film that ends their life. There is no room-temperature figure and none should be assumed. Refrigerate the pack as soon as you get home.
en.fridge: Keep the cluster intact on its base until you cook it, in the original pack or a paper bag, at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 5–7 days is the working limit — borrowed from the general mushroom figure, since nothing is published for shimeji. Leaving the cluster whole genuinely matters: every mushroom you break off is a new cut surface losing water and taking on bacteria. If the pack is sealed plastic and you are keeping them more than a day or two, move them into a paper bag, which lets the moisture escape.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for shimeji, so we do not give one. They can be cut from the base, separated and frozen raw in a flat sealed bag at −18 °C (0 °F), then cooked from frozen — and food held at that temperature stays safe indefinitely. Freezing actually suits shimeji better than most mushrooms, because they are dense and low in moisture, but no quality window has been published and we will not invent one.
en.thawing: Cook shimeji from frozen, straight into a hot pan, a soup or a rice pot. Thawed raw shimeji release water and go limp, and they will steam rather than brown.
spoilage: A slimy or wet film on the caps or stems
Caps gone dark brown and soft rather than firm and springy
The base of the cluster gone black, wet or mushy
A sour or ammonia smell instead of a clean, nutty, earthy one
tips: Keep the cluster whole and cut the base off only when you cook.
Move them from sealed plastic to a paper bag if they are staying more than a day or two.
Do not wash them; brush or wipe instead.
Cook shimeji properly — they are unpleasantly bitter raw or barely cooked, and the bitterness disappears with heat.

faq.q: How long does shimeji last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 5–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, with the cluster intact on its base. That figure is borrowed from mushrooms generally; none is published for shimeji.
No timeline is published, so we do not give one. They freeze raw at −18 °C (0 °F) and cook from frozen, and being dense and fairly dry they take it better than most mushrooms.

faq.q: Why does raw shimeji taste bitter?
faq.a: Shimeji is genuinely bitter until it is properly cooked. Heat drives it off, so give them a real sauté rather than a quick toss.

faq.q: Should you cut off the whole base?
faq.a: Cut off the block of growing medium and any discoloured part just above it. The rest of the stem is good and holds the cluster together while you cook.

zh.name: 鴻喜菇
zh.summary: 鴻喜菇是連著菌床整叢販售的小傘菇，煮熟後質地紮實、帶淡淡堅果味。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照菇類整體來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 5～7 天。
zh.pantry: 鴻喜菇不應該放室溫。和所有鮮菇一樣，它會呼吸也會出水，溫度一高菌傘就變軟，接著出現終結它的那層表面黏膜。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請立刻冷藏。
zh.fridge: 請保持整叢連著根部菌床，用原包裝或紙袋，冷藏於 4°C 以下，約 5～7 天是工作上限——這是比照菇類整體的數字而來，因為鴻喜菇本身沒有公布的數據。保持整叢完整是真的有差：每剝下一朵，就多一個失水、也讓細菌進入的斷面。如果是密封塑膠盒裝而你要放超過一兩天，請改裝進紙袋，讓水氣能散出去。
zh.freezer: 鴻喜菇沒有公布的冷凍保存期限，所以我們不提供數字。它可以從根部切下、撥散後平鋪裝密封袋生凍於 −18°C，使用時不解凍直接下鍋；食品在該溫度下安全上可無限期保存。其實鴻喜菇比多數菇類更適合冷凍，因為它質地紮實、含水量低；但既然沒有公布的品質期限，我們就不編一個。
zh.thawing: 鴻喜菇請不解凍直接下熱鍋、下湯或放進飯鍋。解凍過的生菇會出水變軟，在鍋裡只會冒蒸氣而煎不上色。
spoilage: 菌傘或菇柄上出現黏滑濕答答的薄膜
菌傘轉成深褐並變軟，失去原本的彈性
整叢根部發黑、變濕或糊掉
有酸味或阿摩尼亞味，而不是乾淨的堅果土香
tips: 保持整叢完整，要煮的時候才切掉根部。
要放超過一兩天的話，把密封塑膠盒換成紙袋。
不要洗，用刷的或擦的就好。
一定要確實煮熟——鴻喜菇生的或半生會有明顯苦味，加熱後苦味就消失了。

faq.q: 鴻喜菇放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、保持整叢連著根部，約 5～7 天。這個數字是比照菇類整體而來；鴻喜菇本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有公布的期限，所以我們不給數字。它可以生凍於 −18°C 並不解凍直接下鍋；由於質地紮實、水分少，它其實比多數菇類更耐凍。
鴻喜菇沒煮透時本來就帶苦味，加熱會讓苦味消失。請確實炒熟，不要只在鍋裡翻兩下。
把底下那塊菌床，以及緊鄰上方變色的部分切掉。其餘的菇柄很好吃，也能在料理時幫忙撐住整叢的形狀。
